subject: general
question: Which of the following banks became State Bank of India after nationalisation in the year 1955 and has the largest number of branches in the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Imperial Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Imperial Bank of India (IBI) **was the Indian subcontinent's oldest and largest commercial bank until it was changed into the **State Bank of India in 1955**.
 
• Prior to the foundation of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 1935, it served as the central bank for British India under its royal charter.
 
• The Imperial Bank of India was formed on January 27, 1921, when the three Presidency Banks of colonial India were reorganized and merged into a single banking organization.
 
• The decision of his Majesty's cabinet was undoubtedly inspired by John Maynard Keynes' 1912 book "Indian Currency and Finance."​
 
• **The State Bank of India** is a worldwide public sector bank and statutory organization located in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Bank of India (BOI) **is a nationalized Indian bank. It is owned by the Ministry of Finance of the Government of India, with headquarters at Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex.
 
• Since its nationalization in 1969, it has been held by the government.
 
• SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Inter Bank Financial Telecommunications) is a founding member of BoI, which allows the supply of cost-effective financial processing and communication services.
